subject: Post-call: Nightingale Pay — cost anchors, batching/caching levers & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@nightingalepay.com>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@nightingalepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 16:15:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call: Nightingale Pay — cost anchors, batching/caching levers & next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — good discussion. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to surface the items we agreed to follow up on. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain & goals (what you said)
- High token spend visibility / surprises when enabling helper LLM features in production (chat & classification).
- Budget constraint for Q3: pilot must land under a capped monthly run-rate (target: $12k/mo).
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 350ms for customer-facing chat flows.
- Goal: prove 3–4 feature flows in pilot, then quantify unit economics for a 6–12 month roll.

Cost/TCO anchors we discussed
- Current estimate you shared: ~120M tokens/mo for helper features (batching not in place).
- Break-even math (rough) we sketched: with current model/params, token-only bill ~ $34k/mo; with batching + KV prefix caching we estimate 40–55% reduction in per-token bill for the pilot profile.
- Primary levers: continuous batching for non-interactive inference, prefix KV cache for repeated user/context, and a 4-bit quantized model variant for lower-cost baseline.

Follow-ups (agreed actions)
1) Nightingale: share a one-week sample of anonymized call/chat traffic (token counts by endpoint + percent repeat prefixes) — Priya to send by Wed 07/29. (Attachment: nightingale_cost_model_v1.xlsx placeholder)
2) Redwood: run a pilot-cost projection + two scenarios (conservative: 30% savings, optimistic: 55% savings) based on the sample; include per-feature cost/latency impact. Target deliverable by Thu 07/30. (Attachment: redwood_pricing_v2.pdf)
3) Security/procurement: Priya to confirm SOC2 requirement level and if a vendor questionnaire is required for kickoff.
4) Pilot ops: Rafael/Ben will outline the minimal integration plan (API keys, routing policy, fallback plan) and an ops checklist for a 30-day pilot.

Risks we flagged
- If the sample shows low repeat prefixes, caching upside will be limited and required discounts/commit levels may change the economics.
- High peak concurrency could push to Dedicated capacity earlier than expected (we covered burst options).

Next meeting
- Tentative: Fri 07/31 11:00am ET for a 30-min alignment on data sample and Redwood projection.

If that all looks right I’ll queue the projection run and cc Ben/Rafael on the data once Priya shares it.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-7362

Attachments: nightingale_cost_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing brief stub)

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@nightingalepay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@nightingalepay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Nightingale Pay — cost anchors, batching/caching levers & next steps

Thanks Olga — nice write-up and captures our discussion. A few clarifications:
- The 120M tokens/mo figure is our current estimate across two helper endpoints; I’ll break that down by endpoint and send an anonymized sample.
- We absolutely need the pilot to demonstrate <= $12k/mo run-rate or provide a clear path (discount/commit) to get there — that’s the gating factor for Q3 funding.
- SOC2 type II is required for vendors with onboarding access to PII (we don’t expect you to need PII for the pilot but we’ll confirm).

Priya and I will get the sample over by EOD Wed. If you can include a conservative projection and a path-to-$12k scenario (commit + batching assumptions spelled out) that will be perfect.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Product | Nightingale Pay
samir.k@nightingalepay.com | +1 212-555-0198

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: Nightingale Pay — action items after discovery

Ben/Rafael — copying the external thread for context. Immediate asks:
1) Ben — can you lead the projection? Deliverables: three-line summary (conservative/likely/optimistic savings), a short table showing tokens -> estimated cost post-levers, and a specific path-to-$12k scenario (commit + quantized model + batching parameters). Please flag any assumptions that would materially affect latency SLOs. Aim: draft by EOD Thu 07/30.
2) Rafael — please prepare a 1-page pilot ops checklist (API key flow, routing policy, fallback to hosted model, monitoring hooks we need) and list out any blocking engineering prerequisites on our side (eg: prefix cache setup, model variant availability).
3) I’ll follow up with a concise customer-facing projection pdf and a short SOW template.

Also note: if the sample shows >65% unique prefixes, caching benefit will be small — call that out in the projection.

Thanks — let’s aim to have everything to Samir/Priya by Fri morning so they can present to procurement next week.

Olga
